# v0.49.52

This patch fixes OpenCode 2 sessions that were refused on every turn with `MC-H04` once the conversation held a message without an id, and makes that refusal recover by itself when it still happens.

## Upgrading

Restart your host after updating. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **OpenCode 2: `MC-H04` refused every turn, and `/ctx-recomp` could not clear it (issue 898, thanks @XA21X):** OpenCode 2 sends some messages without an id, such as its step-limit notice and a provider's own compaction checkpoint, and another plugin can add one too. One such message stopped Magic Context from removing the history its summaries already cover. When the conversation without that cut was larger than the model's window, the turn was refused, and every later turn with it. Magic Context now places these messages by the messages around them and makes the cut.
- **A history cut that still cannot be made no longer blocks the session:** when Magic Context cannot tell which loaded messages a summary covers and the request is over the window, it now summarizes further and tries again on the next send. If that cannot make room either, the refusal says what was wrong and what to do (`/ctx-flush` or sending again), in place of advising `/ctx-recomp`, which could not repair that state.
- **Dashboard: dismissing an already dismissed user memory changed its timestamp (issue 900, thanks @soarkit):** a repeated dismiss also told every open session that the user profile had changed. It now does nothing. The dashboard part ships with the next dashboard build.

# v0.49.51

This patch fixes Oh My Pi sessions that were refused on every turn when another extension adds its own instructions to the request, and stops `ctx_search` from repeating a call to a reranking module that is not installed.

## Upgrading

Restart your host after updating. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **Oh My Pi: every turn refused when another extension adds a message (issue 895):** on Oh My Pi 18.18.6, an extension installed from the marketplace runs after Magic Context. Superpowers 7.0.2, for example, adds its startup instructions to each request at that point. Magic Context checks every outgoing request against the one it prepared, took the extra message for conversation history it had not managed, and refused the turn (`expectedRows=3 actualRows=4`). It now accepts up to four short text messages that another extension adds, 32,768 characters in total, as long as they are not content of the session itself and do not sit inside a tool call and its result. Everything else is still refused: restored or altered session history, a changed prepared message, a broken tool pair. One case remains refused, with its own reason (`ambiguous-rewrite`): Oh My Pi rewrites a large untagged message, for example by hiding a secret in a long history summary, and another extension's message sits directly beside it.
- **Oh My Pi: sessions with an `@file` mention are checked on more providers:** such sessions used to skip the comparison of the outgoing request. They are now compared on the Anthropic, Google, Vertex, Gemini CLI, Bedrock, Ollama, OpenAI-compatible Chat and Responses routes, which were verified against Oh My Pi's own encoders. Other routes keep the earlier behaviour.
- **`ctx_search` no longer repeats a refused reranker call (issue 896):** with the Synapse reranker configured but the module absent from the machine's CortexKit daemon, every search retried the call for 30 seconds in the background, about 20 refusals per search, while the search itself had already fallen back after 1.5 seconds. The refusal is now recognized at once and remembered: for 30 seconds the first time, and for 10 minutes when the next check is refused too. A successful call clears it, so a module that was only restarting is used again within 30 seconds. Search results are the same as with reranking unavailable before; only the repeated calls are gone.

# v0.49.50

This patch adds an output-width option for embedding models that support it, stops background runs from retrying a model whose provider said when to come back, and fixes a wrong context-size reading after an Anthropic server-side fallback on OpenCode 2.

## Upgrading

Restart your host after updating. No database migration is needed.

## Added

- **`embedding.dimensions` (issue 405):** an optional output width for OpenAI-compatible embedding models that can return shorter vectors, such as OpenAI's `text-embedding-3-*` and Qwen3-Embedding. Set it to an integer from 1 to 8192 in your user config, and Magic Context sends it as the `dimensions` field of each embedding request. Leave it unset and nothing changes: the request omits the field, and your stored vectors stay valid. Setting or changing it re-embeds your memories and history at the new width, because vectors of different widths can't be compared. Magic Context refuses a response whose width differs from the one you asked for. A project config can't set this option; it is read from your user config only. Thanks to @yiyi-wei for the contribution.

## Fixed

- **Background runs no longer retry a model that is out of quota:** when the summarizer or the dreamer has `fallback_models` and a provider refuses the first model with a time to retry after (a used-up quota window, for example), every later run used to try that model again first, fail, and fall back. Each run left one failed child session and, on OpenCode, an error box in the parent session's terminal. Later background runs now skip that model until the time the provider gave and start on the next one in your list. Your configured order returns after that time, and a successful run on the model clears it at once. When every model in the list is waiting, Magic Context still tries the one that frees soonest. A restart clears this memory, and your own session's requests are never rerouted. It works on OpenCode 1 and on OpenCode 2.2 or newer. Pi and older OpenCode 2 versions don't pass the provider's retry time to plugins, so runs there fall back as before.
- **Context size after an Anthropic server-side fallback on OpenCode 2 (issue 877):** when Anthropic refuses a request on one model and answers it on its fallback model, the reported usage is the sum of both attempts. Magic Context read that sum as the size of the prompt, so one fallback step could look like 110% of the window. The session then held turns, refused them, or summarized early. With the CortexKit anthropic-auth plugin, which records each attempt's usage, Magic Context now takes the size of the attempt that produced the reply. When that record is missing or unreadable, it keeps the previous reading instead of the summed one. Thanks to @iceteaSA for the report and the fix.

# v0.49.49

This patch stops sessions near their context limit from rewriting the prompt for tiny summaries, and keeps Magic Context's per-project working files out of `git status`.

## Upgrading

Restart your host after updating. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **No more tiny summaries near the limit (issue 886):** once a session reached the near-limit band, Magic Context summarized any history that had just left the recent tail, often one or two steps. Each of those summaries changed the cached prompt, so a session sitting in that band rewrote its whole prompt every few steps. A minimum size that should have prevented this never applied. Near the limit, a summary now waits until the history it covers holds at least 2% of the usable window, counting text and tool inputs (tool outputs leave the prompt by other means). Manual `/ctx-wrapup` and `/ctx-recomp`, usage at or above 95%, overflow recovery, and the recovery after switching to a model with a smaller window still summarize whatever is ready, so they never wait. Below the near-limit band nothing changes.
- **Working files no longer show in `git status` (issue 891):** Magic Context wrote its ignore rule into the shared `.cortexkit/.gitignore`, which itself showed up as an untracked file, so `git status` listed `.cortexkit/` after the first summary. Magic Context now writes `.cortexkit/magic-context/.gitignore` containing `*` whenever it creates that folder, for summarizer dumps and documentation proposals alike. It removes its own old entry from the shared file, leaves other tools' entries untouched, and deletes the shared file only if nothing else is left in it. `.cortexkit/magic-context.jsonc` stays trackable. `setup` no longer edits your repository's root `.gitignore`; lines it added before can stay.

# v0.49.48

This patch stops OpenCode sessions from replaying an outdated todo list when the agent uses a custom todo status.

## Upgrading

Restart OpenCode after updating. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **Todo lists with custom statuses are kept (issue 892):** OpenCode's `todowrite` accepts any status or priority text, such as `blocked`, but Magic Context only recognised the four built-in statuses and three priorities. It ignored any other list, so it kept the older list and showed it to the agent as its latest plan whenever the prompt was rebuilt. Magic Context now keeps every list the way OpenCode stores it, and treats every status other than `completed` and `cancelled` as still open. A list it can't read at all clears its saved copy instead of leaving an old one in place. Lists that only use the built-in values are stored exactly as before. Pi is unchanged, because its `todowrite` tool already refuses other values.
